subject: Multi-tenant coverage & pen-test / SOC2 evidence process
messages:
From: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:34:12 -0700
Subject: Clarify pen-test / SOC2 evidence for multi-tenant accounts

Hi Ben / Laura,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Legal and InfoSec at Acme asked for a little more clarity on how Redwood handles audit rights and pen-testing for multi-tenant hosted customers. Two specific asks from their questionnaire:

- Does Redwood allow penetration testing against production systems for multi-tenant customers, or is testing limited to a scoped/non-production environment?
- What is the standard notice period and typical evidence delivery timeline (SOC 2, control mappings, network diagrams, sample logs)?

They also want proposed contract language we can include in our MSA/order form that explicitly states: access windows, ownership of evidence copies, and constraints around co-tenancy. I attached the list of questions from Acme's DSS team for reference (Acme_DSS_review_questions.pdf).

Can you share the standard Redwood approach so we can move this along with legal? Hoping to finalize language this month.

Best,
Tom

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify pen-test / SOC2 evidence for multi-tenant accounts

Hi Tom — thanks for sending this through and for the clear list. I've looped in Laura (product/security ops), Monica (compliance/assurance), and Karthik (legal) so we can provide a concise package you can take to procurement. High level:

- Pen testing: For hosted multi-tenant customers we do NOT allow external testers to run adversarial tests against shared production tenants. Our standard is to provide a scoped non-production environment or an ephemeral staging instance with representative data and topology for vulnerability assessments.

- Dedicated/private deployments: Customers with dedicated tenancy or Private (VPC/on-prem) contracts can run tests in their environment with agreed guardrails; Redwood supports on-site or customer-run pen tests against those instances.

- Notice & evidence timeline: Standard pen-test notice is 30 calendar days for scheduling and coordination; evidence requests (SOC 2 Type II report, control mappings, network diagram, and sampling of logs) are typically fulfilled within 5 business days after request for hosted customers. For more invasive artifact requests or forensic exports we ask for a 10 business day turnaround.

- Contract language: We propose an MSA exhibit that: (1) limits inspection to an isolated environment for multi-tenant customers, (2) reserves Redwood's right to redact operational metadata that would expose other tenants, and (3) defines timeboxed access windows for any live-run testing.

I'll share a quick draft exhibit as an attachment for Acme's team to review; Karthik, can you confirm the redline hotspots we should propose (e.g., "ephemeral staging only" vs "production with strict isolation")?

Tom — I've attached a proposed exhibit draft (redwood-proposed-security-exhibit.docx) with both options and suggested fallback language if Acme needs a stronger commitment (e.g., dedicated staging hours, additional attestations). Would you like a call early next week to walk through the options?

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Clarify pen-test / SOC2 evidence for multi-tenant accounts (internal redlines)

Folks — quick internal note before we send: I reviewed Ben's draft and recommend the following redlines to avoid over-committing on access and evidence scope for hosted customers. Key points to include in the exhibit and order form redline: 

1) Scope: "For multi-tenant hosted customers, penetration testing against production systems is not permitted. Redwood will provide either (a) a staging environment configured to mirror the customer's production topology, or (b) a limited-scope, Redwood-executed vulnerability assessment on production that does not permit injected adversarial tests or lateral movement."

2) Notice & windows: "Customer will provide Redwood with not less than 30 calendar days' notice for penetration testing. Access windows to any Redwood-managed environment will be timeboxed (e.g., consecutive days/hours defined in the SOW) and subject to Redwood's operational policies."

3) Evidence & redaction: "Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report and a control mapping within 5 business days. Any logs or telemetry exports will be redacted to remove information relating to other customers; Redwood will provide sample slices sufficient for customer assurance but will not provide full multi-tenant production exports."

4) Remediation & coordination: "If testing identifies P1/P2 findings, Redwood will propose mitigation timelines and will coordinate a follow-up validation window. For dedicated/private deployments, Redwood will work with the customer to enable broader testing subject to agreed isolation procedures."

5) Operational carve-outs: Include a clause limiting inspection rights where access would materially jeopardize platform availability or other customers' confidentiality. Keep the language "subject to reasonable operational constraints" rather than absolute language.

I'm attaching the redlines as a PDF for Ben to send externally if you want to present a cleaner 'redline vs. clean' package. We should also flag the standard insurance/proof language (we provide our SOC2 in PDF; for attestation queries we can supply SOC2 bridge letters only under NDA).

Karthik

Tom — quick update and proposed next steps:

1) Attached is the final exhibit PDF with our redlines and a clean copy (final-exhibit-redlines.pdf). It reflects Karthik's legal guardrails: no production adversarial testing for multi-tenant hosted customers, 30-day notice, timeboxed access windows, and redaction rules for any production telemetry.

2) Evidence delivery cadence: SOC 2 Type II (latest period) and control mapping — 5 business days after request; targeted exports or forensic logs — up to 10 business days and subject to redaction.

3) For Acme's procurement: if you require production-level pen testing, we can discuss a Private deployment or dedicated staging hours as a paid add-on; I've summarized the two options in Section 3 of the exhibit.

4) Next step: suggest a 30-minute call Monday 11:00am PT to walk through language and confirm which option Acme prefers. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and prepare a short statement of work for the chosen path.
